notes.title: Seven-framework baseline with Leptos 0.8.20
notes.body:
This is the first full seven-framework run, selected before measurement. It adds Leptos 0.8.20 to the existing six production applications. The six-framework 20260922-baseline record and its raw evidence remain unchanged. This run measures commit 47660e5 plus the local benchmark integration; it is a new reference, not an isolated test of a Fusor optimization.

Build: release profile, Binaryen 132 -O3, wasm-bindgen 0.2.117, stripped Wasm names, installed Chrome, and BENCH_SEED=20261004. Both Rust frameworks use the same optimization flags. Leptos lives in an isolated Cargo workspace. SSR uses its official in-order HTML stream collected into a complete string; the methodology documents the direct-string-renderer hydration issue encountered during integration.

All 133 timing metrics, seven memory profiles, and 21 bundle fixtures passed the evaluator. Source and production artifact receipts matched before and after measurement. A separate validation also passed Leptos mount/unmount, keyed edits, event dispatch, server-node-preserving hydration, Hello World, and Todo CRUD/filter behavior in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit; see browser-validation.json.

Leptos has tradeoffs in these workloads: its 10k keyed swap was 0.40 ms and hydration was 28.80 ms, while its 10k shared-source fan-out was 215.50 ms (2.30 ms for 1k). Those are results for these implementations and operations, not a general ranking of applications. Its gzip fixtures were 25.5 KiB (Hello), 63.3 KiB (Todo), and 68.8 KiB (benchmark).

All frameworks returned to the baseline DOM-node count after each cleanup cycle. Leptos retained approximately 7.00 MiB of additional JS heap and 130.25 MiB of Wasm capacity after the large allocation and repeated cycles; Fusor retained approximately 3.50 MiB and 167.56 MiB respectively. Wasm capacity is reserved capacity, not live Rust allocations. These figures do not measure whole-process memory or prove absence of leaks.

Limits: one local Apple M4 Pro, no CPU/network throttling or thermal controls, Chromium timing results, and 15 samples with the maximum as P95. Startup uses fresh browser contexts with a reused browser process. Values below 0.10 ms are below the browser clock floor. The idle development server remained running; builds and other benchmark processes were finished before measurement. Different framework orders, source versions and implementation changes limit direct comparisons with the older run.

Recorded 2026-09-23T22:39:55.622Z on Apple M4 Pro, darwin 24.5.0, browser 153.0.8010.53, 15 samples after 3 warmups.
